# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 40 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 38 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_040_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 40

**1** Jesus said: "A grapevine has been planted outside the Father; and since it has not taken root, it will be pulled up by its roots and will perish."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"Has not taken root"** — LOGOS preferred over PNEUMA's "has no strength." The rooting image is more precise to the agricultural context and explains the weakness.

**"Will perish"** — LOGOS/EMET preferred over PNEUMA's "will die." The Coptic *tako* = to perish/destroy; "perish" carries more eschatological weight.

**Synoptic Parallel:**
- Matt 15:13: "Every plant that my heavenly Father has not planted will be rooted up" — very close; Thomas uses "grapevine" specifically, and "outside the Father" rather than "not planted by the Father."
